mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 9.5% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that may prompt central bank intervention, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to recession fears.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 9.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy approaches a recession.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 and rising unemployment (UNRATE) above 9.5%, the economy is in a supply-driven slowdown phase that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO < 95.0 and UNRATE > 9.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may lead to aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in higher interest rates.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a tightening monetary policy coinciding with a weakening economy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to the dual stress.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises and INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction (HOUST) over the past 3 months signals strong housing market activity that boosts consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST increases, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the employment growth rate (PAYEMS) falls below 50,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months, it indicates a slowing labor market that may lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS < 50,000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.
